rounds.alt: A steep alley of stairs and walls painted in deep blue, with potted plants and tiled steps
rounds.fact: Chefchaouen was founded in 1471 in the Rif mountains. Its blue wash has several origin stories, from Jewish tradition to keeping mosquitoes away, and nobody agrees on one.

rounds.prompt: Where does this noodle soup come from?
rounds.alt: A bowl of curry noodle soup topped with a nest of crispy fried noodles, with chopsticks and a spoon
rounds.fact: Khao soi is a coconut curry noodle soup crowned with crispy fried noodles, the signature dish of Chiang Mai and northern Thailand. Its roots are usually traced to Chinese Muslim traders from Yunnan.

rounds.alt: Huge steel spheres lit with small lights, joined by tubes, seen from below at dusk
rounds.fact: The Atomium was built for the 1958 World's Fair: nine steel spheres arranged like a cell of an iron crystal, magnified 165 billion times.

rounds.prompt: Where would you find this little figure?
rounds.alt: A small bronze figure with outstretched arms standing at the foot of a white wall
rounds.spotLabel: Name what these little statues are called
rounds.fact: Hundreds of bronze dwarfs hide around Wrocław. They began as a nod to the Orange Alternative, a 1980s movement that mocked the communist government with absurd street happenings and painted dwarfs.

rounds.prompt: A friend who lives there sends you this. Where are you meeting?

postcard.text: Che, nos vemos el domingo en La Bombonera. Llevá la camiseta azul y oro.

rounds.fact: "Hey, see you Sunday at La Bombonera. Bring the blue and gold shirt." La Bombonera, the chocolate box, is Boca Juniors' stadium in La Boca, named for its steep, boxy stands.

rounds.alt: A worn street of tall colonnaded buildings with a green 1950s car driving past
rounds.fact: Cuba's 1950s American cars have been kept running for decades through the trade embargo with improvised parts, and many now work as taxis. Centro Habana sits between Old Havana and Vedado.

credit.title: Vintage car driving in Centro Havana (Unsplash)
credit.author: Eva Blue

rounds.prompt: Where does this pizza come from?
rounds.alt: A blistered round pizza with tomato, melted white cheese and a few basil leaves
rounds.fact: The margherita is said to be named after Queen Margherita of Savoy, who visited Naples in 1889. The craft of the Neapolitan pizzaiuolo is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.

rounds.alt: Two identical steel skyscrapers joined by a bridge, between other towers under a blue sky
rounds.fact: At 452 m, the Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004. A two-storey skybridge joins them at the 41st and 42nd floors.

rounds.alt: A weathered stone corner building with a long enclosed wooden balcony on carved stone brackets
rounds.fact: Valletta's closed wooden balconies, gallariji, let people watch the street unseen while keeping out the sun. The city was built by the Knights of St John after the Great Siege of 1565.

rounds.prompt: A friend who lives there sends you this. Where are you meeting?

postcard.text: 道頓堀のグリコの看板の前で7時に会おう！

rounds.fact: "Let's meet at 7 in front of the Glico sign on Dōtonbori!" The Glico running man has lit up the Dōtonbori canal in Osaka since 1935.

rounds.alt: Brightly painted houses along a canal with wooden mooring posts and a tall leaning bell tower behind
rounds.fact: Burano is a lagoon island of Venice where every house is painted a bright colour, and owners ask permission before repainting. The bell tower of San Martino leans visibly.

rounds.prompt: Where does this dish come from?
rounds.alt: Sliced roast duck with glossy skin beside a bamboo steamer of thin pancakes, dark sauce, spring onion and cucumber
rounds.fact: Peking duck is roasted until the skin turns glassy, then carved at the table and wrapped in thin pancakes with spring onion, cucumber and sweet bean sauce. Beijing's oldest duck restaurants date back to the 1400s.

credit.title: 2016-08-27 Peking Duck at Great Wall Restaurant Beijing anagoria
credit.author: Anagoria

rounds.alt: A statue with outstretched arms on a mountain peak above a sea of clouds at sunrise
rounds.fact: Christ the Redeemer has stood 30 m tall on Corcovado mountain since 1931, made of reinforced concrete clad in soapstone tiles.

rounds.alt: A row of tall, narrow wooden gabled houses painted ochre, white and red
rounds.fact: Bryggen's wooden warehouses were the Hanseatic League's trading post in Bergen, dealing mostly in dried cod. Rebuilt after many fires on the old pattern, they are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

rounds.prompt: A friend who lives there sends you this. Where are you meeting?

postcard.text: Tukutane Forodhani saa kumi na mbili jioni, tule mishkaki baharini.

rounds.fact: "Let's meet at Forodhani at six this evening and eat skewers by the sea." Forodhani Gardens on Stone Town's waterfront turns into a street-food market every evening.

rounds.alt: A hillside crowded with brightly painted houses under a grey sky
rounds.spotLabel: Name one of the city's hills (cerros)
rounds.spotName: Any of its 40-odd cerros, like Cerro Alegre
rounds.fact: Valparaíso is built on more than 40 hills, linked by century-old funicular lifts called ascensores. Its historic quarter is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

rounds.prompt: Where does this dish come from?
rounds.alt: A boat-shaped bread filled with melted cheese, a runny egg yolk and a pat of butter
rounds.fact: Adjaruli khachapuri comes from Adjara on Georgia's Black Sea coast. The boat shape is no accident: you tear off the crust and stir the egg and butter into the cheese.

credit.title: Khachapuri Adjaruli with egg and butter
credit.author: Eugene Krasnaok

rounds.alt: A tall pale concrete church with stepped columns, a bronze statue in front and snow on the ground
rounds.fact: Hallgrímskirkja's 74.5 m tower was designed to echo the basalt columns that form when lava cools. The statue out front is Leif Erikson, a gift from the United States in 1930.

rounds.alt: Two buildings covered in teal and patterned ceramic tiles on a wet cobbled street
rounds.fact: Graça is one of Lisbon's oldest neighbourhoods, high on one of the city's seven hills. Glazed azulejo tiles became popular on façades in the 1800s because they shrug off damp and heat.

rounds.prompt: A friend who lives there sends you this. Where are you meeting?

postcard.text: Tere! Kohtume kell kuus Raekoja platsil, Vana Toomase all.

rounds.fact: "Hi! Let's meet at six on Town Hall Square, under Old Thomas." Vana Toomas is the weathervane guard on top of Tallinn Town Hall, keeping watch over the square since 1530.

rounds.alt: A railway line running down a narrow lane, with houses and doorways right up against the tracks
rounds.spotName: Train Street (off Lê Duẩn and Phùng Hưng)
rounds.fact: Hanoi's Train Street is a row of houses built right up to a working railway laid by the French in the early 1900s. When a train squeezes through, residents step back into their doorways.

rounds.prompt: Where does this fish stew come from?
rounds.alt: A bowl of orange fish stew with a mussel, pieces of white fish and chopped herbs
rounds.fact: Bouillabaisse began as the stew Marseille fishermen made from the bony rockfish they couldn't sell. In 1980 the city's chefs signed a charter setting out what a true one must contain.

rounds.prompt: Where is this facade carved into the rock?
rounds.alt: A tall classical facade with columns, carved straight out of a pink sandstone cliff
rounds.fact: Al-Khazneh was carved out of the sandstone by the Nabataeans around the 1st century AD, probably as a royal tomb. Its name, the Treasury, comes from a legend that pirates hid gold in the urn at the top.

rounds.alt: A pale green panelled door between white columns, under a fanlight window in a red brick wall
rounds.fact: Dublin's Georgian doors, framed by columns and topped with fanlights, date from its 18th-century building boom. Henrietta Street, laid out in the 1720s, is the oldest Georgian street in the city.

rounds.prompt: A friend who lives there sends you this. Where are you meeting?

postcard.text: Servus! Treffen wir uns um acht beim Riesenrad im Prater?

rounds.fact: "Hi! Shall we meet at eight by the Ferris wheel in the Prater?" German is spoken in several countries, but +43 is Austria. Vienna's Riesenrad has turned over the Prater since 1897.

rounds.alt: A narrow street of pink and yellow colonial houses with wooden balconies and bougainvillea
rounds.spotLabel: Name the walled part of the city
rounds.fact: Cartagena's old town sits inside about 11 km of stone walls built against pirates and rival navies. Its wooden balconies date mostly from the colonial era, when it was Spain's great Caribbean port.

credit.title: Balconies, Street scene in Cartagena, Colombia (24745444421)
credit.author: Joe Ross from Lansing, Michigan

rounds.prompt: Where does this rice bowl come from?
rounds.alt: A hot stone bowl of rice topped with vegetables, sprouts, a raw egg yolk and sesame
rounds.fact: Bibimbap means "mixed rice": rice topped with vegetables, chilli paste and often an egg, stirred together at the table. Jeonju is its most famous home and holds a bibimbap festival every year.

rounds.alt: A weathered stone temple gallery with a tall, carved tower rising behind it
rounds.fact: Angkor Wat was built in the early 12th century for King Suryavarman II, first as a Hindu temple to Vishnu, later Buddhist. It is the largest religious monument in the world, and it appears on Cambodia's flag.

credit.title: 2016 Angkor, Angkor Wat, Brama Angkor Wat (30)
credit.author: Marcin Konsek

rounds.alt: A wall of broken white tiles set with square panels of patterned ceramic, under pink roses
rounds.fact: This patchwork of broken tiles is trencadís, the mosaic style Antoni Gaudí made famous. He covered Park Güell's benches, walls and dragon in it between 1900 and 1914.

credit.title: Trencadís. Park Güell
credit.author: Andrew Moore from Johannesburg, South Africa

rounds.prompt: A friend who lives there sends you this. Where are you meeting?

postcard.text: Akşam yedide Galata Kulesi'nin önünde buluşalım mı? Sonra Karaköy'de balık yeriz.

rounds.fact: "Shall we meet in front of Galata Tower at seven? Then we'll eat fish in Karaköy." The stone tower has stood over the Golden Horn since the Genoese built it in 1348.

rounds.alt: A terrace of flat-roofed houses painted pink, mint, lilac and yellow on a sloping street
rounds.fact: Bo-Kaap, on the slopes of Signal Hill, grew from the 1760s as home to Cape Malay families, many descended from people enslaved from Southeast Asia. Its brightly painted houses are among Cape Town's oldest.

credit.title: Bo-Kaap - Cape Town, South Africa (3883775540)
credit.author: South African Tourism from South Africa

rounds.prompt: Where do these tacos come from?
rounds.alt: A hand holding a paper tray of small soft tacos filled with marinated pork, onion and coriander
rounds.fact: Tacos al pastor grew from the shawarma Lebanese immigrants brought to Mexico: pork marinated in chilli and achiote, cooked on a vertical spit and served with pineapple. They became a Mexico City staple in the 1960s.

rounds.alt: A white castle with slender towers on a forested crag, below a steep grey cliff
rounds.fact: King Ludwig II of Bavaria began Neuschwanstein in 1869 as a private retreat and died before it was finished. It opened to visitors weeks after his death in 1886 and is said to have inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty castle.

rounds.alt: Two paths running through tunnels of closely spaced vermilion gates with black bases
rounds.fact: Fushimi Inari Taisha is lined with thousands of vermilion torii gates, each donated by a business or person whose name is written on the back. The paths climb about 4 km up Mount Inari.

credit.title: Double torii path at Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine, Kyoto, Japan
credit.author: Basile Morin

rounds.prompt: A friend who lives there sends you this. Where are you meeting?

postcard.text: نتقابل في خان الخليلي الساعة سبعة؟ هنشرب شاي في الفيشاوي.

rounds.fact: "Shall we meet at Khan el-Khalili at seven? We'll have tea at El Fishawy." Arabic is spoken in over 20 countries, but +20 is Egypt. Cairo's great bazaar dates from the 14th century.

rounds.alt: A wide street paved with polished pale stone between uniform stone houses, with a bell tower at the far end
rounds.fact: Stradun, the main street of Dubrovnik's walled old town, was rebuilt after the great earthquake of 1667, which is why its houses look so alike. Its limestone is polished smooth by centuries of footsteps.

rounds.prompt: Where does this pizza come from?
rounds.alt: A thick-crusted pizza in a deep pan, with tomato and pepperoni over a tall golden edge
rounds.fact: Chicago deep-dish is baked in a tall, oiled pan, with the cheese under a layer of chunky tomato so it doesn't burn in the long bake. Pizzeria Uno claims to have invented it in 1943.

rounds.alt: Gilded spires and tiered pavilions around a marble terrace, with people walking barefoot
rounds.fact: The Shwedagon's main stupa rises about 99 m over Yangon, its gold plates crowned with thousands of diamonds and rubies. Legend says it holds eight hairs of the Buddha.

rounds.alt: Tall, narrow brick houses with stepped and bell-shaped gables along a canal with a moored boat
rounds.fact: Amsterdam's 17th-century canal ring is lined with tall, narrow merchant houses that lean slightly forward, so goods hoisted on the beam at the top swing clear of the windows. It became a World Heritage Site in 2010.

credit.title: DSC00288, Canal Cruise, Amsterdam, Netherlands (338955340)
credit.author: Lyn Gateley from Silicon Valley, CA, USA

rounds.prompt: A friend who lives there sends you this. Where are you meeting?

postcard.text: Allô! On se rejoint au marché Jean-Talon vers midi? J'apporte des beignes.

rounds.fact: "Hi! Shall we meet at Jean-Talon Market around noon? I'll bring doughnuts." +1 covers the US and Canada, but 514 is Montreal, and beignes is Quebec French. The market has run in Little Italy since 1933.
